events.description: Reagan-Gorbachev working luncheon discussing Afghanistan withdrawal, national reconciliation, and Geneva accords.
Working luncheon between Reagan and Gorbachev with delegations at the White House, 12:40-2:10 PM, following Oval Office meeting that ended 12:15 PM.
Reagan urged Gorbachev to press Vietnam to withdraw from Cambodia.
Gorbachev stated Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan was linked to an end of US support for the Afghan opposition from the date withdrawal begins.

Shultz said the US was ready to reaffirm support for the Geneva agreements, resolving non-interference; the missing piece was a withdrawal timetable. Under the accords US support would cease 60 days after withdrawal begins.
Working group meeting on Afghanistan, with Shultz and Shevardnadze discussing the outcome afterward.

Shultz and Gorbachev agreed that after the summit the sides would begin work on practical measures with the parties concerned; Gorbachev proposed Afghanistan and other regional issues be mentioned in the Joint Statement.

relationships.detail: Reagan and Gorbachev held a working luncheon in the Family Dining Room of the White House during the Washington summit.
relationships.quote: SUBJECT: Working Luncheon with General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev

relationships.detail: Shultz and Shevardnadze discussed the outcome of the working group on Afghanistan and the Soviet welcome of US reaffirmation of the Geneva agreements.
relationships.quote: as he and Foreign Minister Shevardnadze discussed following the meeting of the working group yesterday, the Soviet side welcomed American readiness to reaffirm support for the Geneva agreements

relationships.detail: Shultz and Gorbachev debated linkage between Soviet troop withdrawal, national reconciliation and cutoff of US support for the Afghan opposition.
relationships.quote: Gorbachev responded that Soviet withdrawal was definitely linked to an American obligation to cut off support for opposition forces

relationships.detail: Gorbachev is accompanied by Foreign Minister Shevardnadze; Shevardnadze supports the Soviet position that there is no linkage between withdrawal and reconciliation and proposes adding Central America to the statement.
relationships.quote: Foreign Minister Shevardnadze remarked that there was no linkage "in effect" between troop withdrawal and national reconciliation.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev said the Soviet side would tell Najib that creation of a coalition government was the Afghans' own affair.
relationships.quote: the Soviet side would tell Najib-- and the American side should do the same with the opposition forces--that the creation of a coalition government was their affair

relationships.detail: The Afghan opposition forces receive US financial and military support, which Gorbachev demanded be cut off when Soviet withdrawal starts.
relationships.quote: the United States could continue financial and military support for the opposition forces

relationships.detail: Najib is the leader of the Afghan government to whom the Soviets would deliver the message.
relationships.quote: the Soviet side would tell Najib

relationships.detail: Soviet troops are in Afghanistan supporting the Kabul government; Gorbachev says new Afghanistan should not be led by a pro-Soviet government.
relationships.quote: did not want the new Afghanistan to be led by either a pro-American or a pro-Soviet government

relationships.detail: Soviet troops are deployed in Afghanistan pending withdrawal.
relationships.quote: Soviet troops would no longer engage in military operations

relationships.quote: the President emphasized to Gorbachev the necessity of Vietnamese withdrawal from Cambodia

relationships.detail: The two governments negotiated Afghanistan language for the Joint Statement and the Geneva process.
relationships.quote: Gorbachev then proposed that the Joint Statement on regional issues mention that Afghanistan was discussed.

key_claims: Gorbachev insisted Soviet withdrawal be linked to an end of US support for the Afghan opposition from the date withdrawal begins.
Shultz said the Soviet view now delinked withdrawal from national reconciliation, allowing Geneva to focus on a withdrawal timetable.
Under the Geneva accords as Shultz described, US support would cease 60 days after withdrawal begins.
Gorbachev said Afghanistan should be neutral and nonaligned, led by neither a pro-American nor pro-Soviet government.
The US reaffirmed support for the Geneva accords, which the Soviets said resolved the non-interference issue.
